A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HPL framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, curriculum and loss ablations, sub-task analyses, and agent case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, reports three-seed performance summaries, and adds measured resource comparisons.

M1.justification: Behavior cloning, preference-pair generation, the four segmentation strategies, curriculum stages, and composite objective remain unchanged. Section 3.1 clarifies the existing exploration/offline-optimization sequence; new Algorithm 1 restates the existing scheduler.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ALFWorld, WebShop, and InterCode-SQL with the same task coverage. The resource comparison uses existing ALFWorld coverage, and the new apple-cleaning walkthrough is an illustration rather than an additional evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SFT, RFT, ETO, IPR, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, the base models, and the same HPL variants. The new resource comparison reuses existing methods without changing membership in the retained performance comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix D.5 adds resource measurements for ALFWorld/Qwen2.5-1.5B, including call counts and generation/training times, with training timings on four A800 GPUs. Existing splits, accuracy metrics, backbones, and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. The newly stated five MC rollouts per group is additional disclosure, not an established budget revision.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5/Table 5 adds a supplementary analysis of computational costs across baselines and HPL variants. The curriculum and loss ablations, phase-wise curves, sub-task breakdowns, and empirical case studies are retained unchanged after relocation or renumbering.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point estimates without reported repetition information to three-seed means with ± values for the fine-tuned methods across both model scales. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting for the central comparison. The meaning of ± remains unspecified, and v1's unstated run count prevents inferring an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: The central performance estimates and margins are extensively revised: the 7B HPL Semantic average changes from 67.81 to 67.28, while its ALFWorld-unseen margin over IPR changes from 8.96 to 5.97 points. These are updated three-seed summaries, with the principal superiority finding retained. Table 5 adds resource results; existing ablation and sub-task values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and its full bias-variance derivation are unchanged, moving from Appendix D to Appendix G. The new reward-estimation walkthrough and scheduler pseudocode explain existing mathematics without introducing a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the criticism of step-level DPO as a finite-data, limited-rollout difficulty and clarify that offline optimization follows one-shot exploration. The central contributions—hierarchical preferences, the dual-layer curriculum, and superiority on three benchmarks—remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains segmentation as a structural prior and grouping as a response to limited-rollout noise. It explicitly acknowledges that sufficiently expressive step-level DPO can represent the same long-horizon credit assignment asymptotically. The original limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly announces a code-and-data release with a repository address, specifies five MC rollouts per group, and documents parallel sampling, resource costs, and timing hardware. These additions materially extend reproducibility information beyond v1's existing hyperparameter tables and prompts; repository availability is supported only by the PDF's statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to GenSim, Yulan-OneSim, and a test-time-scaling survey, with a short discussion distinguishing training from inference-time strategies. It also clarifies HPL's relationship to ETO/IPR's data-collection protocol and online PPO, while retaining the main related-work structure.

P1.justification: Targeted revisions affect the abstract, motivation, and results discussion. v2 adds a problem-setting subsection, explanatory appendices, reproducibility statement, and acknowledgments, and updates affiliations and publication headers. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds resource Table 5 and Algorithm 1, adapts Table 1 to display ± values, revises Figure 1's caption, and relocates several displays. Existing figures and other tables retain their visual content; appendix sub-task tables are simply renumbered.

improvement.justification: Three-seed reporting makes the main comparisons more assessable, while the explicit exploration/offline distinction, rollout-count disclosure, and code/data access information improve clarity and reproducibility. The gains remain limited by undefined ± statistics, unchanged point-only ablations, and resource accounting that labels selected pipeline components rather than establishing total end-to-end costs.
